findings.title: float: right on .small-action button is ignored now that .small-action is a flex container
findings.body: This PR adds `@include flexbox()` to `.small-action`, but the `button` rule inside it still relies on `float: right` to pin the small-action undo/recover button to the right edge of the row. Floats have no effect on flex items, so the button will now render immediately after the `.small-action-desc` text instead of at the far right of the row whenever the description is short (e.g. "closed the topic"). The header change in this same PR solves the equivalent problem for `.panel` by adding `margin-left: auto`; the same fix (or `justify-content: space-between`) is needed here for the button.

findings.title: margin-left: auto used to right-align .panel does not work in the 2009-spec flexbox fallback the new mixin emits
findings.body: `.panel` is now pushed to the right edge of the header with `margin-left: auto` instead of `float: right`. The `flexbox()` mixin added in this PR emits `display: -webkit-box`/`display: -moz-box` as fallbacks, and in that 2009 flexbox spec (old iOS Safari, old Android stock browser) auto margins on box children are treated as 0, so on exactly the browsers those fallback lines exist for, the header panel (user menu / login / signup buttons) will sit immediately after the logo instead of at the right edge. At the same time the float fallbacks were removed (`.title { float: left }` deleted, `.panel { float: right }` deleted), so those engines get the degraded layout with no fallback. Either drop the old-spec prefixes or add a fallback such as `-webkit-box-pack: end` / keeping a float fallback.

findings.title: align-items mixin passes standard keywords verbatim to legacy properties that use different value names
findings.body: The new `align-items($alignment)` mixin copies its argument into `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, but those legacy properties do not accept the standard `flex-start`/`flex-end` keywords — they expect `start`/`end`. The mixin compiles silently and the declaration is simply dropped by those engines, so the first time someone uses `@include align-items(flex-start)` (the most common value in real layouts) alignment will be silently broken in old WebKit and IE10. Current usages only pass `center`/`baseline`, which happen to be valid in both syntaxes, so this is latent rather than an active bug — but the mixin should map the values (or the limitation should be documented) since it is being introduced for codebase-wide reuse. Additionally, `-ms-align-items` on line 121 is not a property that exists in any browser (IE10's 2012 spec only has `-ms-flex-align`), so that line is dead code.

findings.title: Bullet category badge in the scrolled header loses its 5px top offset with no replacement
findings.body: This PR removes `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }`. That offset was what aligned the small inline-flex bullet badge with the topic title text in the header's extra-info (scrolled) state. The new `@include align-items(center)` is applied to `.d-header .contents`, which only centers the `.extra-info-wrapper` as a whole within the header bar; `.extra-info-wrapper` itself is not a flex container and the badge inside it still uses `float: left`, so nothing replaces the intra-wrapper alignment the 5px margin provided. In the scrolled header the category bullet badge will sit higher than the title text baseline. The added `line-height: 1.5` does not compensate for the badge-to-title alignment. This should be verified in the scrolled header and either kept or replaced with an equivalent adjustment.
